pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Legenda Aurea, De Sancta Lucia
pairs.question: Soror mea Lucia, virgo Deo devota, quid a me petis, quod ipsa poteris praestare continuo matri tuae?
pairs.answer: Nam ecce per fidem tuam sanata est.
pairs.derivation: Agatha's vision-speech to Lucia: a rhetorical question she answers herself within the same utterance. Question runs to the interrogative '...matri tuae'; the original has a comma there, normalized to '?'. Answer is the immediately following sentence in the same speech. No framing to drop (speech is introduced by narration 'stantem et dicentem sibi:' which is excluded).

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Legenda Aurea, De Sancta Lucia
pairs.question: Qui sunt corruptores corporis et mentis?
pairs.answer: Corruptores mentis vos estis, qui suadetis, ut animae suum deserant creatorem. Corruptores vero corporis sunt, qui corporalem delectationem praeponunt epulis sempiternis.
pairs.derivation: Paschasius asks (interrogative 'qui sunt'), Lucia answers. Dropped speech tags 'Respondit Paschasius:' and 'Lucia dixit:'. Source terminal '!' normalized to '?'. Answer is Lucia's full two-sentence reply, both directly defining the two kinds of corruptores asked about; quoted contiguously.

pairs.locus: Iacobus de Voragine, Legenda Aurea, De Sancta Lucia
pairs.question: Quae sunt illa maleficia, quod una puella a mille viris non moveretur?
pairs.answer: Non sunt ista maleficia, sed beneficia Christi.
pairs.derivation: Paschasius asks (interrogative 'quae sunt'), Lucia answers. Dropped speech tags 'Tunc dixit Paschasius:' and 'Lucia dixit:'. Source terminal "'" (a stray closing mark) normalized to '?'. Answer stops at the first full stop; what follows ('Porro si adhuc decem milia adhibueris...') elaborates/digresses and is cut.
